payload.title: Italy Wedding Packages and What They Include
payload.audience: Australian couples, late 20s to 40s, AUD 40k to 150k+, comparing Italy packages and working out what's actually included before they enquire
payload.reader: An Australian couple (or the parent helping pay) who has already decided on Italy, has two or three package pages open in different tabs with 'from' prices that don't line up, and wants to know what each price actually buys, what sits outside it (guest rooms, legal paperwork, flights, planner fee, exchange rate) and what to ask before sending an enquiry.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor: request a Wedded Concierge consultation to have an Italy package costed in AUD on the couple's own dates and guest count, with inclusions confirmed in writing.
payload.angle: Most page-one results list packages or quote a headline 'from' price; few explain what that price is built on. This guide takes a package apart as a planner reads it: (1) the venue offer, which typically covers ceremony and reception spaces with set-up and is priced for a set guest count on a standard date; (2) the 'may include' list, which is indicative until it is confirmed in writing for your date; (3) what usually sits outside the package, such as guest rooms booked separately, civil or symbolic ceremony paperwork, travel, transfers and the exchange rate. It ends with a like-for-like comparison checklist so a couple can line up three Italy packages before enquiring, and explains plainly how Wedded Concierge handles the gaps (AUD quotes, fee agreed in writing, inclusions confirmed in writing before you commit, guest room blocks with Wedded Privileges).
must_include: A direct answer within the first 100 words: what an Italy wedding package usually covers and what it usually doesn't, written for a phone reader.

Anatomy of a package, using the structure of our own Italy package pages (ceremony venues, reception venues, accommodation, 'upgrades available', a from price for a guest range) as the illustration. Describe the structure in our words; do not lift the inclusion wording on the Cappuccina draft, which partly derives from a competitor page.

What a 'from' price means: where the offer starts for a set guest count on a standard date, and that a Wedded Advisor costs it on the couple's dates, guest count and season. Any AUD figure must be written 'From AUD ...' and flagged [[VERIFY: Nic sign-off]]; prefer no specific figure unless Nic signs off.

What usually sits outside the package: guest accommodation booked separately, legal ceremony paperwork (link to the Italy legal guide), flights and transfers, extra events (welcome aperitivo, recovery lunch), marquee or wet-weather plans, and currency exposure.

A comparison checklist (table or list) of questions to put to any package: guest count the price assumes, date type and season, which spaces are exclusive, wet-weather plan, music curfew or end time [[VERIFY per venue]], who supplies celebrant, florals and photography, how guest rooms are held, payment schedule and currency.
Package vs fully planned vs DIY: honest trade-offs, pointing to Wedded Concierge (/wonderland-concierge) for planned and Wedded Marketplace (/marketplace) for couples making their own arrangements.

How Wedded Concierge works, using only brand-facts claims: one Wedded Advisor start to finish, advisor in the couple's time zone quoting in AUD, fee agreed in writing before work begins, inclusions confirmed in writing before the couple commits, suppliers paid at standardised industry rates, guest room blocks with Wedded Privileges.

Internal links down the cluster: /destinations/europe/italy (venues and ready-made offers), /expert-advice/how-much-does-a-wedding-in-italy-cost (budgets), /expert-advice/getting-married-in-italy-the-complete-legal-guide-for-destination-couples (legal), /expert-advice/can-you-get-married-in-a-tuscan-villa, and /privileges. Link to package pages only once live (Cappuccina is noindex).
avoid: 'All inclusive', 'no hidden costs' or 'everything included' (brand-facts pricing rules).
Any bare price, non-AUD price, or price without Nic's sign-off flag; never reuse the Cappuccina comparison prices or the competitor's figures.
Naming, quoting or paraphrasing Easy Weddings or any competitor's package copy, inclusion lists or claims.
Turning the guide into a cost guide: per-guest budgets and regional cost ranges belong to /expert-advice/how-much-does-a-wedding-in-italy-cost. Summarise in one line and link.
Turning it into a legal guide: one short section and a link to the legal guide.
A list of venues or a 'best packages' roundup (that is the job of /destinations/europe/italy).
'17 years' of relationships, number of weddings planned or any statistic not on a checked live page; 'within one business day' response time; the 30% savings claim from the older Italy article.
Clichés (fairytale, dream day, say I do in paradise), stacked superlatives, exclamation marks, em dashes.
Linking to /packages/italy/tuscany/cappuccina-country-resort while it is noindex/draft.
